title: Why Do Skyscrapers Hide a Giant Ball Inside?
description:
Near the top of Taipei one oh one, one of the tallest buildings in the world, hangs a golden steel ball weighing about six hundred and sixty tonnes. It is not decoration. It swings. When a typhoon hits Taiwan, the ball moves against the building's sway and calms it down. Today, eleven parts of a skyscraper, and why each one exists, starting with that giant ball.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 11 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:01 1. The giant steel ball
2:08 2. The top that moves
3:16 3. The steps that confuse the wind
4:19 4. The twisting tower
5:22 5. The building fixed in secret
6:42 6. The concrete core
7:47 7. The giant arms at the top
8:43 8. The sky lobby
9:55 9. The red lights on top
10:56 10. The machine that cleans the windows
11:53 11. The piles under the tower
12:59 The verdict

Sources:
- Taipei 101 tuned mass damper (660 t, floors 87-92, ~1 m movement in Typhoon Soudelor 2015): Wikipedia, "Taipei 101" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taipei_101 ; Wikipedia, "Tuned mass damper" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuned_mass_damper
- Building sway, occupant comfort criteria, wind tunnel testing: CTBUH (Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat) https://www.ctbuh.org/ ; RWDI wind engineering
- Burj Khalifa ("confusing the wind", Y-shaped plan, 828 m, 192 piles 1.5 m x 43 m, cathodic protection, BMUs): Skidmore, Owings & Merrill; Wikipedia, "Burj Khalifa" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burj_Khalifa ; Baker, Korista et al., "Engineering the World's Tallest - Burj Dubai" (CTBUH 2008)
- Shanghai Tower (632 m, 120° twist, ~24% lower wind loads): Gensler; Wikipedia, "Shanghai Tower" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Tower
- Citicorp Center 1978 crisis (bolted joints, quartering winds, night welding, revealed 1995; 400 t tuned mass damper): Joe Morgenstern, "The Fifty-Nine-Story Crisis", The New Yorker, 29 May 1995 ; Wikipedia, "Citigroup Center" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citigroup_Center
- Cores, outriggers, refuge floors: CTBUH technical guides ; Wikipedia, "Outrigger (architecture)"
- Sky lobbies, rope length limit and KONE UltraRope: KONE https://www.kone.com/en/ultrarope ; Wikipedia, "Sky lobby" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_lobby
- Aircraft warning lights: FAA Advisory Circular 70/7460-1 "Obstruction Marking and Lighting" https://www.faa.gov/
- Building maintenance units: Wikipedia, "Building maintenance unit" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Building_maintenance_unit
